chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, who said:
Someone narrated to me from the one who asked him about a man who forgets the two rak'ahs of the obligatory prayer until he leaves, so he said: He appoints another.
Ibn Muskan said: And in another hadith, if he has passed the miqat of the people of his land, then let him return and pray them.
For Allah, the Exalted, says: “And take from the مقام of Ibrahim a place of prayer.”

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ: the two rak'ahs that are due to be performed
key_terms.مِيقَاتَ: the appointed boundary or limit passed in travel
key_terms.يُوَكِّلُ: he appoints someone as a deputy

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets the two rak'ahs and leaves before performing them?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for one who forgets the two rak'ahs associated with the obligation until after departing. It indicates either deputizing another or returning to perform them, and it cites the Qur'anic command concerning the مقام of Ibrahim as support for this ruling.
